_meta.indication: ExEm Foam is an ultrasound contrast agent indicated for sonohysterosalpingography to assess fallopian tube patency in women with known or suspected infertility.

pivotal_trials.phase: Not applicable; published diagnostic performance literature study submitted under 505(b)(2)
pivotal_trials.design: Nonrandomized, observational, single-center study; patients imaged first with HyFoSy then laparoscopy with chromopertubation as reference standard
pivotal_trials.population: Women evaluated for subfertility scheduled for laparoscopy with dye
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Agreement of HyFoSy compared to laparoscopy with chromopertubation (reference standard)
pivotal_trials.result: Agreement between HyFoSy and laparoscopy diagnoses was 100%; statistical reviewer calculated sensitivity 100% (95% CI: 73% to 100%) and specificity 100% (95% CI: 90% to 100%)

pivotal_trials.phase: Not applicable; prospective observational diagnostic performance study submitted under 505(b)(2)
pivotal_trials.design: Prospective, observational study comparing 2D-air/saline-HyCoSy, 2D/3D-HyFoSy, and 2D/3D-HDF-HyFoSy against laparoscopy with dye
pivotal_trials.population: Sexually active women ages 21 to 40 with history of infertility without prior tubal patency evaluation
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Diagnostic accuracy (sensitivity/specificity) of HyFoSy versus laparoscopy with dye reference standard

key_safety: Common adverse reactions are pelvic and abdominal pain; vasovagal reactions and associated symptoms such as nausea and faintness; and post-procedure spotting. There is a risk of post-procedure gynecological infections when used in sonohysterosalpingography.
target_moa: An ultrasound contrast agent: a foam created by mixing the kit components is instilled into the uterus and appears echogenic (white) inside the fallopian tube; when the tube is patent the foam travels through the tube and spills into the peritoneal cavity, enabling visualization of tubal patency.
modality: other (ultrasound contrast agent / intrauterine foam kit)

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee convened; application did not raise significant safety/efficacy issues unexpected for the class and there were no controversial issues warranting discussion.

basis.text: Application was reviewed as Standard (not Priority).

summary.text: ExEm Foam was approved November 7, 2019 as an original 505(b)(2) NDA (NDA 212279) with standard review, relying on published literature for evidence of safety and effectiveness; no accelerated approval, breakthrough, fast track, orphan, or priority designations were applied, and the application was not referred to an advisory committee.

citations.quote: your amendments, submitted pursuant to section 505(b)(2) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FDCA) for ExEm Foam (air polymer-type A) intrauterine foam.

Your application for ExEm Foam was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because outside expertise was not necessary; there were no controversial issues that would benefit from advisory committee discussion.
